transcript: People are not talking nearly enough about the new theater facility in upper Manhattan. I remember when this was announced several years ago, and it's so funny, cause I was literally just in this area the other day and thinking to myself, huh, it's been a while since we've had an update on that project. Little did I know that it was few days away from opening. It's called the People's Theatre Centro Cultural Inmigrante, and the idea is that it's geared specifically toward immigrant stories and immigrant communities. This is an evolution of the People's Theatre Project, which has existed for a long time as a theatre company. Now this performing arts facility is its new permanent home. The first theater production they're doing is a return engagement of Manuel Oliver's solo play Guac, which had a brief run at the Public a couple years ago, and it played Woolley Mammoth. They also have a cabaret from Robin De Jesus and Linedy Genao A Conversation Series, the first of which features both of the writers of in the Heights. And in addition to the fact that this is obviously a really cool, admirable mission in general, one of the many reasons I'm excited for this is that, you know, I live in upper Manhattan, and I know that there is very little theater up here. I'm actually not aware of any venues above like 125th st. in Manhattan that regularly house professional live theatre. But please, do tell me If I'm wrong, I'd love to know. Either way, though, it's gotta hold the new record for the northernmost theatre venue in Manhattan. It's up in Inwood, off the 207th st. 1 station.
